subject: VAT liability split and VAT ID validation for Omnicart billing
body:
From: Sara Klaas <sara.klaas@omnicart.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Johan Vermeer <johan.vermeer@omnicart.com>, procurement@omnicart.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Question on VAT treatment & proration for multi-entity purchase

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — Omnicart is keen to move forward. Before procurement signs, two tax questions came up from our finance team:

1) We purchase seats for teams across multiple EU subsidiaries. Can Redwood issue a single invoice and have the EU reverse-charge applied to the entire amount, or do we need separate invoices per local entity? We want to avoid manual invoice splitting if possible.

2) For mid-month seat increases (proration), how will VAT be calculated and displayed on the invoice? Our AP team needs clear VAT lines for partial-period charges.

I attached our VAT registration certificate for the Netherlands entity (omnicart_vat_cert_2026.pdf). Please confirm what evidence Redwood needs to treat this as a B2B reverse-charge (0% VAT) transaction. Also looping in procurement (procurement@omnicart.com) — they will prepare the PO once we have clarity.

Best,
Sara
Sara Klaas
Head of Finance, Omnicart BV

---

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klaas <sara.klaas@omnicart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@omnicart.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question on VAT treatment & proration for multi-entity purchase

Hi Sara — thanks for sending the certificate and for the clear questions. Helpful to loop Ben and Lauren in so we can cover tax validation and invoice formatting. Summary of what we recommend and the evidence we need: 

- VAT ID validation: we need the VAT number (NL#######B01 style) and legal entity name. We validate via VIES. If VIES returns valid we will apply reverse-charge (0% VAT) and include the buyer VAT number on the invoice with the note: "Reverse charge — Article 194 (Council Directive 2006/112/EC)".

- Invoicing approach for multi-entity purchase: two options (please confirm preference):
  1) Single consolidated invoice to Omnicart BV (your Dutch entity) with reverse-charge applied for the whole invoice. This is simplest but requires that Omnicart BV is the contracting and receiving entity for the service (legal purchase order + VAT ID).
  2) Split invoices per bill-to entity (recommended if different subsidiaries are paying from separate AP ledgers). Redwood can generate separate invoices; we will need the billing contacts and VAT IDs for each entity.

- Proration / partial-month seat increases: we will calculate prorated amounts at the net (pre-VAT) level, show a prorated net line and then show VAT (0% or local VAT depending on validation). For consolidated billing with reverse-charge, the VAT line will be 0% but we will still show the gross-to-net math so your AP can reconcile. I attached a sample proration layout (proposed-invoice-proration.xlsx).

Next steps from our side: 
- Ben will confirm VIES validation logic and fallback if VIES is temporarily unavailable.
- If you prefer option (1) consolidated billing, please confirm the legal entity name that will sign the contract and the VAT number to use. If you prefer (2), please send the billing contacts and VAT IDs for each subsidiary.

I will also open a quick billing ticket to ensure our invoice generation flags the reversed-charge reason field so your AP system can map it automatically.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-invoice-proration.xlsx (sample invoice layout)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Sara Klaas <sara.klaas@omnicart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@omnicart.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question on VAT treatment & proration for multi-entity purchase

Hi all — quick technical note on how our billing engine will handle this: 

1) VAT ID Validation:
   - Primary: VIES (EU VAT Information Exchange System) lookup. If VIES returns "valid", we store the VAT ID string + timestamp and mark customer as B2B-validated.
   - Secondary (if VIES down or returns invalid): request one of the following pieces of evidence — national VAT registration printout, certificate (you already attached one), or a recent invoice showing the VAT number. If still unresolved, we apply local VAT to the invoice and place a short payment hold until the customer provides valid evidence.

2) Reverse-charge logic:
   - For B2B-validated EU customers where place-of-supply is the buyer's country, we emit VAT rate 0% for the goods/service lines and include this invoice note: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient (Art. 194 2006/112/EC)."
   - We also populate a machine-readable tax code in our invoice JSON so ERP integrations can map automatically (field: taxTreatmentCode = "RC_EU_B2B").

3) Multi-entity and proration handling:
   - If consolidated billing chosen: billing entity must be contractual buyer. All prorated charges are calculated on net values and aggregated; VAT shown as separate line per legal requirement.
   - If split invoices chosen: prorations are computed per entity based on seat allocations passed in the order payload (we accept a CSV with seat-to-entity mapping).

4) Edge cases & fallback:
   - If VIES reports the VAT ID as valid but the legal name differs slightly, we accept a reasonable name match and require a short attestation email from the finance contact.
   - If the country requires local withholding (rare for SaaS in NL), that is a separate AP process; we can flag the invoice with a note but Redwood doesn't automatically withhold. Please confirm if Omnicart expects withholding instructions.

I'll attach a short checklist for the tax ops team (vat-validation-checklist.docx) and can prepare a one-off invoice preview once you confirm consolidated vs split.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Tax & Billing Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vat-validation-checklist.docx

Hi Avery / Ben,

Thanks — procurement confirms we will proceed with consolidated billing to Omnicart BV (Dutch entity). We have attached the signed PO and the national VAT certificate (see omnicart_vat_cert_2026.pdf). We will complete the DocuSign contract using the Dutch entity as the contracting party (link sent in separate email).

A quick follow-up: in the Netherlands, AP sometimes requires a local VAT statement on the invoice for internal entries. Can you include the VIES validation timestamp and the reverse-charge note as a discrete invoice field (not buried in the footer)? That will help our accounts payable automation.

Also, confirm whether Redwood needs any seat-to-entity mapping for historical billing (we plan to consolidate future purchases under the Dutch entity).

Best,

procurement@omnicart.com
